content.title: Repeating the Sins of Qaum-e-Lut: How to Protect Our Society!
content.subtitle: Health Warnings, Moral Reflection, and Protecting the Next Generation
content.body:
In the Western world, same-sex marriage and LGBTQ culture have long gained institutional recognition in the name of so-called “personal freedom” and human rights. Through legal recognition, educational curricula, and international corporate campaigns, these practices have increasingly been presented as a normal part of life. More concerning, however, is that in our religious and conservative Bangladesh, this is no longer a distant issue. Under the guise of modernity and progress, these ideas are quietly challenging the foundations of our society and families.

The Quiet Spread of Homosexuality in Bangladesh and Recent Developments

Despite legal and social restrictions, several concerning incidents related to homosexuality have come to public attention in recent years. In May 2017, RAB detained 28 young men during a raid at a community centre in Atibazar, Keraniganj, Dhaka, reportedly recovering a large quantity of drugs. The incident brought widespread attention to the alleged presence of an organised, clandestine network.

Later, in December 2023, the Detective Branch reportedly arrested several groups accused of using the Grindr app to lure people in Mirpur and Dhanmondi, record intimate videos, assault victims, and demand ransom. Similarly, in July 2024, a college student in Chawkbazar, Chattogram, was reportedly lured to an apartment through a gay dating platform and held hostage for blackmail.

Controversies surrounding the inclusion of transgender and gender identity concepts in national textbooks have also raised concerns among some families about the protection of religious and cultural values.

Serious Health Risks in the Light of Medical Science

  • Higher Risk of HIV/AIDS: According to the World Health Organization (WHO) and international health agencies, men who have sex with men face a significantly higher risk of HIV infection than the general population. Receptive anal intercourse can damage sensitive tissue, increasing the risk of infection through exposure to infected blood and bodily fluids.

  • Mpox Outbreaks: During recent global outbreaks of mpox, a substantial proportion of reported cases occurred among gay and bisexual men, particularly within certain sexual networks.

  • Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs): Infections such as syphilis, gonorrhoea, and chlamydia can spread through sexual contact, including among men who have sex with men.

  • Cancer Risks Associated with HPV: Human papillomavirus (HPV) can increase the risk of anal cancer. Certain HPV infections are also associated with other cancers.

  • Hepatitis Infections: Hepatitis A and B can spread through sexual contact, including practices involving exposure to infected bodily fluids, and may cause serious liver damage.

  • Physical Complications: Some sexual practices may cause anal injuries. Repeated or severe injuries can lead to lasting complications, including problems with bowel control.

The Fate of Qaum-e-Lut in the Light of the Qur’an

In Islamic tradition, the people of Prophet Lut (AS) were among the first to engage in sexual acts between men that the Qur’an condemns. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, describes their wrongdoing in the Holy Qur’an:

“Do you commit such an outrage as no one in the world has ever committed before you? You lust after men instead of women. You are indeed a transgressing people.”

(Surah Al-A‘raf: 80–81)

Despite repeated advice and warnings, they did not abandon their actions. Consequently, Allah’s punishment came upon them, and their towns were overturned as stones of baked clay rained down upon them (Surah Hud: 82).

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also warned that when immorality becomes widespread among a people, epidemics and new diseases may emerge among them that were unknown to their ancestors (Sunan Ibn Majah: 4019).

Ways to Protect Ourselves from This Destructive Path

  1. Repentance and Psychological Support: Anyone struggling with distress or confusion about their sexuality should not lose hope in Allah’s mercy. They can seek spiritual guidance and, if needed, consult a qualified mental health professional for compassionate support. Sexual orientation itself is not a mental disorder, and attempts to forcibly change it can cause harm.

  2. Digital Boundaries and Healthier Company: Avoid harmful online interactions, exploitative dating platforms, and groups that encourage unsafe behaviour. Step away from relationships that pressure you into actions against your values, and seek the company of trustworthy, practising Muslims.

  3. Guarding One’s Gaze and Making Halal Choices Easier: Unrestrained viewing of explicit content can expose people to harmful influences. Protect your eyes from online obscenity and practise responsible digital habits. Parents should also make marriage easier for their children when they are ready and willing.

  4. Family Awareness and Islamic Guidance: Build open, trusting relationships with children so they feel safe discussing emotional struggles without fear. Teaching Islamic values, modesty, and good character from an early age is an important responsibility for every family.

footer_button.hint: Surrendering blindly to desires and rejecting divine guidance can lead society toward moral decline. From an Islamic perspective, the path forward lies in reaffirming Tawheed and returning to the foundation of faith: La ilaha illallah. This declaration is not merely a ritual or a matter of counting recitations. It represents a lifelong commitment to free ourselves from the servitude of our desires and recognise Allah’s sovereignty alone. Our Kalima Campaign was launched to revive the spirit of Tawheed among Muslims worldwide. Its purpose extends beyond a particular day or promotional campaign. It seeks to rekindle sincere faith in every heart. You, too, can join us in this spiritual journey of renewal for the Ummah.
